1.

Learned AGA accepts notice for respondent Nos.1 to 3.
2.

The petitioner, who belongs of Department of Health and Family Welfare Services, was deputed to work as Designated Officer as Food Safety Officer under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'the Act') in BBMP East Zone, K.R.Circle vide order dated 03.09.2024 for a period of one year.

entities.text: Department of Health and Family Welfare Services
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. Alleging that the petitioner has been prematurely repatriated vide order dated 07.05.2025, the petitioner had approached the Karnataka Appellate Tribunal.

The Appellate Tribunal, after considering the case of the petitioner, rejected the interim prayer sought for on the ground that the tenure of deputation was only one year and once the tenure is completed, the petitioner cannot claim to continue to be deputed after the completion of the tenure.
NC: 2025:KHC:39351-DB HC-KAR 4.

The submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner is required to be granted the benefit of continuity of service and protection against the transfer on the ground the deputation has to be for minimum five years.

5. Learned Additional Advocate General submits that a policy decision having been taken, the Sub-Divisional Officer has been designated as the officer under the Act and as such, the Health Officers, who had been deputed have been repatriated.
The policy decision having been so taken, the petitioner cannot claim any benefit.

6. The submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the deputation could have been only for a period of five years in terms of the order dated 16.07.1983 at Annexure-A1 and there could be no delegation for a period lesser than five years.

7. We are unable to accept the same since the order of deputation dated 03.09.2024, under which the petitioner claims, categorically indicates that the same was only for NC: 2025:KHC:39351-DB Dr V Shivegowda vs State Of Karnataka on 30 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26518804/
3 HC-KAR a period of one year.

entities.text: NC: 2025:KHC:39351-DB Dr V Shivegowda vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If at all the petitioner had any grievance against the same, the petitioner ought to have raised it at that time and not after repatriation pending being upheld.
The same in our considered opinion is completely mischievous and is not sustainable.
8. In that view of the matter, no ground being made out, the writ petition stands dismissed.

9. However, considering that the petitioner is suffering from liver cancer, in the event of there being any transfer, the submission of learned AAG that the priority for transfer or appointment in Bengaluru would be considered as per the Karnataka State Civil Services (Regulation of Transfer or Medial Officers and Others Staff) Rules, 2025 is placed on record.

entities.text: Karnataka State Civil Services (Regulation of Transfer or Medial Officers and Others Staff) Rules, 2025
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 10. In view of disposal of the petition, pending applications stand disposed of.
